code: diagnostics <- fiscal_diagnostics(indicators) diagnostics #> Fiscal indicator diagnostics #>   Indicators: 11  #>   Redundant pairs: 3  #>   Near-zero variance: 0  diagnostics$redundancy_pairs #>               var1                   var2          r #> 1     op_reserve_z liquid_assets_months_z  0.9295005 #> 2    debt_assets_z               equity_z -0.9403921 #> 3 surplus_margin_z       profit_predepr_z  0.9566320

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_triage() turns diagnostics auditable recommendation: indicators retain dimension estimation, keep standalone measures, drop redundant noise. triage keeps one indicator redundant pair. recommendations three business-model indicators follow correlations: two expense shares correlate , rules can retain dimension estimation (form small “spending mix” dimension), self-sufficiency, correlates nothing, flagged standalone noise. statistical rule tell whether indicator measures construct . three describe spending pattern revenue model rather financial condition, override recommendations exclude :
code: triage <- fiscal_triage(diagnostics) triage$decisions[, c("variable", "decision", "reason")] #>                  variable   decision #> 1         days_cash_ops_z     retain #> 2            op_reserve_z  redundant #> 3  liquid_assets_months_z     retain #> 4           debt_assets_z  redundant #> 5                equity_z     retain #> 6        surplus_margin_z     retain #> 7        profit_predepr_z  redundant #> 8         return_assets_z     retain #> 9              prog_exp_z     retain #> 10       expenses_admin_z     retain #> 11            self_suff_z standalone #>                                                                                                        reason #> 1                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 2                                                 Provisional drop from a highly correlated redundancy group. #> 3                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 4                                                 Provisional drop from a highly correlated redundancy group. #> 5                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 6                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 7                                                 Provisional drop from a highly correlated redundancy group. #> 8                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 9                                                               Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 10                                                              Eligible for multivariate dimension modeling. #> 11 Low communality; retain as a possible standalone indicator rather than forcing it into a shared dimension. triage <- fiscal_triage(   diagnostics,   overrides = c(prog_exp_z = "noise", expenses_admin_z = "noise",                 self_suff_z = "noise") ) triage$selected_for_dimensions #> [1] "days_cash_ops_z"        "liquid_assets_months_z" "equity_z"               #> [4] "surplus_margin_z"       "return_assets_z" triage$retained_standalone #> character(0)

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_dimensions() uses PCA (exploratory factor analysis) propose empirical dimensions retained indicators. nfactors NULL, parallel analysis chooses number. discovers describes groupings; name — call. Reserves solvency indicators form one dimension; margin return indicators form . Name content:
code: dimensions <- fiscal_dimensions(   indicators,   triage = triage,   method = "pca",   seed   = 42 ) #> Parallel analysis suggests that the number of factors =  NA  and the number of components =  2 dimensions #> Fiscal dimension discovery #>   Method: PCA  #>   Dimensions: 2 ( parallel ) #>   Multi-indicator dimensions: 2  #>   Cross-loading indicators: 0  #>   Unassigned indicators: 0 dimensions$assignments[, c("variable", "primary_dimension", "primary_loading")] #>                 variable primary_dimension primary_loading #> 1        days_cash_ops_z        Dimension1       0.6922338 #> 2 liquid_assets_months_z        Dimension1       0.8898898 #> 3               equity_z        Dimension1       0.7687656 #> 4       surplus_margin_z        Dimension2       0.9192845 #> 5        return_assets_z        Dimension2       0.9556156 a <- dimensions$assignments perf <- a$primary_dimension[a$variable == "surplus_margin_z"] dimension_names <- setNames(   ifelse(dimensions$multi_indicator_dimensions == perf, "performance", "resilience"),   dimensions$multi_indicator_dimensions ) dimension_names #>    Dimension1    Dimension2  #>  "resilience" "performance"

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_health_fit() freezes reviewed dimensions scoring specification. fitted object stores indicator orientation (inferred fiscal_metrics() directions), centers, scales, missing-value treatment, dimension coefficients — everything needed score new data identically later.
code: fit <- fiscal_health_fit(indicators, dimensions = dimensions,                          dimension_names = dimension_names) fit #> Fitted fiscal-health measurement model #>   Dimensions: 2  #>   Standalone indicators: 0  #>   Reference observations: 5892  #>   Missing-value rule: median

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_health_score() applies fitted model. parameters re-estimated; just transforms combines indicators dimension scores (prefixed fh_). model frozen, fit can score different panel year scale.
code: scored_dims <- fiscal_health_score(indicators, fit)  grep("^fh_", names(scored_dims), value = TRUE) #> [1] "fh_resilience"           "fh_performance"          #> [3] "fh_resilience_coverage"  "fh_performance_coverage" round(cor(scored_dims$fh_resilience, scored_dims$fh_performance, use = "complete.obs"), 2) #> [1] 0.36

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_weights() defines dimension scores standalone indicators combine composite. default equal weighting; min_coverage controls much observation’s weighted inputs must present receives score.
code: weights <- fiscal_weights(fit, min_coverage = 0.5) weights #> Fiscal-health weights #>   Method: equal  #>   Measures: 2  #>   Missing-score rule: reweight  #>      measure measure_type original_weight weight #>   resilience    dimension               1    0.5 #>  performance    dimension               1    0.5

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: fiscal_health_index() produces single composite score (coverage column recording much information score based ).
code: indexed <- fiscal_health_index(scored_dims, weights)  summary(indexed$fiscal_health) #>     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max.  #> -2.50353 -0.59180 -0.02616  0.00000  0.54486  2.95750

title: The fiscal health workflow
text: reviewed triage dimensions, fiscal_health() runs mechanical stages — fit, score, weight, index — one call: deliberately automate diagnostics, triage, dimension discovery, stages require substantive review.
code: result <- fiscal_health(indicators, dimensions = dimensions,                         fit_args = list(dimension_names = dimension_names)) result #> Fiscal-health result #>   Mode: fit_and_score  #>   Observations: 5892  #>   Dimensions: 2  #>   Standalone indicators: 0  #>   Composite index: yes

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_current_ratio() Measures short-term liquidity comparing current assets current liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range current ratio bounded zero unbounded . Values 1.0 mean current liabilities exceed current assets. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,150, 15, organizations clustered 0.5 5. Benchmarks rules thumb 1.0: Conventional adequacy threshold – liabilities exactly covered. 0.5: Indicates acute short-term risk (Tuckman & Chang 1991). 3.0-4.0: May indicate excess cash slow receivables collection. Sector medians generally fall 1.0,2.51.0, 2.5 range (Zietlow et al. 2007). Calculated : 990 filers .
code: cr = current_assets / current_liabilities  current_assets      = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable                       + inventories + prepaid_expenses current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_quick_ratio() Measures liquidity using liquid assets, excluding inventory prepaid expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range quick ratio bounded zero (asset values negative properly prepared balance sheet) unbounded . practice empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,100, 10, extreme values 5 typically indicating cash hoarding, unusually large receivables balance, organization minimal current liabilities (e.g., grant-making foundation accounts payable). Values zero can occur net receivables negative (allowances uncollectible pledges exceed gross pledges) denominator carries accounting adjustments. large values can result current liabilities near zero, producing ratios mathematically valid practically uninterpretable. default winsorization 1st/99th percentiles addresses extremes. Benchmarks rules thumb 1.0: Conventionally adequate; liquid assets cover current liabilities. 0.5-1.0: Potential short-term stress. 0.5: Common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). high values (3-5) may signal excess cash hoarding rather financial health. declining trend consecutive years stronger warning signal single year’s value. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: qr = quick_assets / current_liabilities  quick_assets        = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_liquidity_ratio() Measures immediate liquidity using cash cash equivalents current liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero unbounded . ratio 1.0 means cash exactly covers current payables. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,200, 20, values 0.1 5.0. high values common grant-making foundations endowed organizations carry minimal accounts payable. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.5: Organization cover half near-term payables cash alone; reliant receivables collection borrowing. 1.0 : Full cash coverage current liabilities. highly conservative measure, values somewhat 1.0 normal receivables healthy. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: casr = ( cash + savings ) / current_liabilities  current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

what: Cash and Savings to Assets Ratio
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_assets_ratio() Cash savings share total assets; measures liquid composition asset base. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1: zero means liquid assets; one means entire asset base cash savings. practice nonprofits fall 0.05,0.500.05, 0.50 range. Values 0.60 uncommon operating nonprofits may indicate excess cash hoarding. Benchmarks rules thumb universally accepted benchmark. Values 0.05 suggest minimal liquid cushion; values 0.60 may indicate -deployment assets toward mission. Foundations endowed institutions naturally show higher ratios operating nonprofits. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: cash_assets = ( cash + savings ) / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_on_hand() Absolute dollar amount cash liquid savings held end year. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Cash hand bounded zero (negative properly prepared balance sheet) unbounded . Unlike ratio measures, scale dollars, comparison across organizations different sizes requires normalization. Use get_months_cash_operations() get_days_cash_operations() size-adjusted comparisons. Benchmarks rules thumb absolute measure, benchmarks depend organization’s expense base. common practitioner rule least 60-90 days operating expenses liquid cash. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends minimum three months operating expenses accessible reserves. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: coh = cash + savings

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_burn_ratio() End--year cash relative beginning--year cash; measures whether organization drawing accumulating cash position. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero (cash negative). Values 1.0 indicate cash depletion; values 1.0 indicate cash accumulation. Ratios near zero indicate near-complete cash exhaustion. ratio undefined (NA) beginning--year cash zero, occurs first year operation complete cash drawdown. Benchmarks rules thumb ratio consistently 1.0 multiple years warning sign; single year 1.0 may reflect planned reserve spending. 0.50 single year (cash halved) warrants investigation. ratio consistently 1.0 indicates accumulating liquidity reserves. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: cash_burn = cash_eoy / cash_boy

what: Days of Operating Cash on Hand
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_days_cash_operations() Measures many days organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero unbounded , expressed days. typical range nonprofits approximately 0,3650, 365. Values 365 (one year cash) indicate large liquid reserves relative expenses, uncommon operating nonprofits typical foundations. Benchmarks rules thumb 30 days: Generally considered distress indicator. 60-90 days: Commonly cited minimum threshold (Nonprofit Finance Fund). 90-180 days: Considered healthy operating nonprofits. Healthcare nonprofits typically benchmarked 150+ days due longer receivables cycles. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: doch = liquid_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_assets = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable daily_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

what: Days of Operating Cash and Investments
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_days_cash_investments() Measures days operating coverage using liquid investment assets, net fixed property obligations. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions. Negative values occur unrestricted net assets negative (accumulated deficits exceed equity) fixed assets net debt exceed liquid resources. Values 365 indicate one year coverage. Benchmarks rules thumb 180-365 days: Considered solid reserve position endowed organizations. large gap metric get_days_cash_operations() indicates liquidity concentrated investments rather accessible cash. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: doci = investable_assets / daily_expenses  investable_assets = unrestricted_net_assets + investments                     - ( land_buildings_equipment + mortgages_payable ) daily_expenses    = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

what: Months of Operating Cash on Hand
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_months_cash_operations() Number months organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero; unbounded . typical operating range nonprofits approximately 0,240, 24 months, values 12 months uncommon operating organizations (typical foundations). Benchmarks rules thumb Less 1 month: Acute liquidity risk. 1-3 months: adequate; common guidance least 3 months. 3-6 months: Generally considered healthy operating nonprofits. 6+ months: Strong reserve position. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends 3-6 months target. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: moch = liquid_assets / monthly_expenses  liquid_assets    = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable monthly_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 12

what: Months of Liquid Unrestricted Net Assets (LUNA)
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_liquid_assets_months() Number months organization can operate using liquid unrestricted net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions, expressed months. Negative values indicate fixed property (net mortgage debt) exceeds unrestricted net assets. practical range operating nonprofits approximately −12,36-12, 36 months. Benchmarks rules thumb general benchmarks get_operating_reserve_ratio() (expressed years rather months): 3-6 months considered adequate operating nonprofits. Negative LUNA values particularly informative: indicate unrestricted equity entirely absorbed illiquid fixed assets. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: luna = liquid_unrestricted_net_assets / monthly_expenses  liquid_unrestricted_net_assets = unrestricted_net_assets                                  - ( net_fixed_assets - mortgages_payable ) monthly_expenses = total_expenses / 12

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_assets_ratio() Proportion total assets financed liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Theoretically bounded 0,10, 1 net assets positive: zero means debt; one means liabilities equal total assets (zero net assets). Values 1.0 occur total liabilities exceed total assets, .e., organization negative net assets (accumulated deficits exceed equity). distress indicator uncommon capital-intensive nonprofits (hospitals, housing) carrying large long-term debt. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: Generally considered financially stable. 0.50-0.70: Moderate leverage; manageable warrants monitoring. 0.70: High leverage; common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). 1.0: Negative net assets; acute financial risk. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: dar = total_liabilities / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_equity_ratio() Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero liabilities non-negative unrestricted net assets positive. Unbounded unrestricted net assets small. Values zero occur unrestricted net assets negative (accumulated deficits exceed unrestricted equity), acute financial distress signal. ratio undefined (NA) unrestricted net assets equal zero. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 1.0 mean total liabilities less unrestricted equity base – generally considered strong. Values 1.0 3.0 indicate moderate leverage. Values 5.0 indicate high leverage relative equity base common vulnerability threshold. Negative values indicate negative unrestricted net assets, almost always signals significant financial stress. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: der = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_netassets_ratio() Compares total liabilities total net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero total net assets positive; unbounded net assets approach zero. Negative values occur total net assets negative (liabilities exceed assets), insolvency signal, ratio monotone financial health across zero. ratio undefined (NaN) total net assets equal zero. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 1.0 mean liabilities smaller net asset base. Values 3.0-5.0 commonly flagged high leverage nonprofit vulnerability literature. Always read alongside get_debt_equity_ratio(), uses unrestricted net assets: large gap two means much equity cushion donor restricted. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: dnar = total_liabilities / total_net_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_shortterm_ratio() Measures short-term obligations share total net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero net assets positive. Negative values occur net assets negative (accumulated deficit), makes ratio uninterpretable burden measure. Unbounded net assets approach zero. Typical values financially stable nonprofits 0,0.300, 0.30 range. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 0.10 indicate modest short-term payables relative equity base – comfortable position. Values 0.30 suggest near-term obligations placing meaningful pressure net assets. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: stdr = short_term_liabilities / net_assets  short_term_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_secured_ratio() Secured mortgages notes payable share total liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. nonprofits zero secured debt; capital-intensive organizations (housing, healthcare, higher education) can show values 0.70. Benchmarks rules thumb standard benchmark. informative tracked time compared within subsectors similar capital structures. organizations high secured debt ratios, lenders scrutinize collateral value debt service coverage ratio. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: debt_secured = secured_mortgages_notes / total_liabilities

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_unsecured_ratio() Unsecured notes loans payable share total liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. nonprofits carry unsecured notes, distribution highly concentrated zero long right tail. Benchmarks rules thumb established benchmark. Presence unsecured debt inherently negative – many healthy nonprofits use lines credit cash flow management – large growing ratio warrants scrutiny. Trend analysis informative single year’s value. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: debt_unsecured = unsecured_notes_loans / total_liabilities

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_equity_ratio() Share total assets financed net assets (equity). Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Theoretically bounded 0,10, 1 net assets positive. Values 1.0 possible. Values zero occur net assets negative (accumulated deficit), distress indicator. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0.10,0.950.10, 0.95. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: Equity finances half assets – generally healthy. 0.30: High leverage; common capital-intensive subsectors. useful trend measure: declining values warrant investigation. Transform. rank-based inverse normal transform maps empirical mid-ranks onto Gaussian. Tied values (block exact zeros, say) share score middle block, reference distribution keeps winsorized tail observations, clipped values scored actual quantile rather extreme normal score. preserves ordering distances, robust almost shape — cost discarding original spacing.  bimodal shape (strongly negative kurtosis) pulled toward single normal mode.
code: set.seed(3) x_rank <- c(rnorm(1000, -3), rnorm(1000, 4))   # bimodal, mixed support  fit <- find_best_normalization(x_rank, range = "np", verbose = FALSE) c(type = fit$transform_type,   raw_kurt = round(fit$raw_kurtosis, 2), fit_kurt = round(fit$fit_kurtosis, 2)) #>          type      raw_kurt      fit_kurt  #> "rank_normal"       "-1.75"       "-0.16"  plot_normalize_x(x_rank, range = "np")

title: Panel smoothing
text: given window size N (must odd): Beginning panel — use first N observations. Middle panel — use symmetric window centered observation, including (N - 1) / 2 lags (N - 1) / 2 leads. End panel — use last N observations. guarantees two things: every observation replaced smoothed value, panel dimensions remain unchanged.

title: Panel smoothing
text: Within window, observations can weighted three ways.

title: Panel smoothing
text: values window receive equal weight. N = 3:

title: Panel smoothing
text: focal observation receives 50% weight; remaining 50% distributed evenly among neighbors. N = 3 centered:

title: Panel smoothing
text: Weights decline geometrically distance focal observation, following half-life rule (1, 1/2, 1/4, …) normalized sum one. Centered (N = 3): (0.25, 0.50, 0.25) Edge (N = 3): (0.5714, 0.2857, 0.1429)

title: Panel smoothing
text: Missing values dropped within window. remaining weights re-normalized still sum one. every value window missing, result NA. example, window {2, NA, 4} weights {0.50, 0.25, 0.25} collapses {2, 4} re-normalized weights {0.667, 0.333} (.e. 0.50 / 0.75 0.25 / 0.75), giving 2.667.

title: Panel smoothing
text: Take organization , variable x = 1, 2, 3, 4, window = 3. Equal weights — smoothed value simple mean window: giving c(2, 2, 3, 3). Half weights — edges shift half-weight boundary value: giving c(1.75, 2.00, 3.00, 3.25). Decay weights — geometric decay focal point: giving approximately c(1.5714, 2.0000, 3.0000, 3.4286). examples reproduce values x column.

title: Building a 990 panel
text: get_panel() downloads multiple years IRS 990 e-file data stacks one long-format panel, stamping row TAX_YEAR (optionally) attaching Business Master File metadata. rest article use small hand-built panel mimics messiness real e-file data — amended returns, group returns, gap:
code: # a four-year panel with the default financial tables panel <- get_panel(years = 2019:2022)  dim(panel) table(panel$TAX_YEAR)  # skip the BMF join (faster; attach later with merge_bmf()) panel <- get_panel(years = 2019:2022, include_bmf = FALSE) mk <- function(ein, yr, grp = "", amd = "", stamp, rev) {   data.frame(     EIN2 = ein, TAX_YEAR = yr,     RETURN_GROUP_X = grp, RETURN_PARTIAL_X = "", RETURN_AMENDED_X = amd,     RETURN_TIME_STAMP = stamp,     F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT = rev, F9_09_EXP_TOT_TOT = round(rev * 0.9),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }  panel <- do.call(rbind, list(   mk("A", 2019, stamp = "2020-05-01", rev = 500000),   mk("A", 2020, stamp = "2021-05-01", rev = 520000),   mk("A", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 560000),   mk("B", 2019, stamp = "2020-05-01", rev = 300000),   mk("B", 2019, amd = "X", stamp = "2020-09-01", rev = 310000),  # amended duplicate   mk("B", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 340000),             # 2020 missing   mk("C", 2020, grp = "X", stamp = "2021-05-01", rev = 800000),  # group return   mk("C", 2020, stamp = "2021-05-20", rev = 810000),   mk("C", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 790000) ))  knitr::kable(panel[, c("EIN2", "TAX_YEAR", "RETURN_GROUP_X",                        "RETURN_AMENDED_X", "F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT")])

title: Building a 990 panel

Ask per-ID classification table return_classification = TRUE: organization labelled persistent, entrant, exit, transient, empty, panel_spell seamless segmented (segmented spell gap year). attach columns data instead, use append_classification = TRUE; panel_summary() reports overall shape panel: Keep organizations want analyze panel_filter_types() — example, persistent organizations, observed first last year window (possibly gaps , like B): panel_impute() can fill short internal gaps selected panel types smoothing scoring:

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics

Four versions per metric — raw, winsorized (_w), standardized (_z), percentile rank (_p), outliers scale never distort comparisons. One-call scoring — compute_all() appends every metric data frame. Sensible 990 defaults, overridable — function defaults correct e-file field names accepts column names. Pipe-enabled form-aware — handles full 990 990-EZ filers; blank financials interpreted correctly via sanitize_financials(). title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Downloads multiple years IRS 990 efile data stacks single long-format panel, stamped TAX_YEAR. Retrieval delegated panel990::panelize(); Business Master File metadata attached afterwards unless include_bmf = FALSE.
code: # Retrieve a 4-year panel with default tables (P00, P01, P08, P09, P10, P11, P12, A01) panel <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022 )  dim( panel ) table( panel$TAX_YEAR )  # Retrieve without BMF metadata (faster; attach manually later) panel <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022, include_bmf = FALSE )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: IRS 990 efile data can contain multiple filings per organization per year (amended returns, partial-year returns, group returns). deduplicate() reduces panel one record per EIN2 × TAX_YEAR using three ordered heuristics: Drop group returns — RETURN_GROUP_X == "X" Drop partial-year returns — RETURN_PARTIAL_X == "X" Keep recent — retain filing latest RETURN_TIME_STAMP applying drop rule eliminate records organization-year, records rescued passed next step. function wrapper around panel990::panel_deduplicate() prints short summary row counts ; use inspect_duplicates() detailed breakdown duplicate filings type.
code: panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel )  # Suppress the summary panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel, verbose = FALSE )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Applies centered rolling window average within organization’s time series reduce year--year noise financial variables. Returns data frame identical dimensions column names — selected numeric columns replaced smoothed values. vars argument selects columns smooth: Three weighting schemes available:
code: # Full panel workflow panel       <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022 ) panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel )  # Smooth PZ-scope financial fields with a 3-year window panel_smooth_pz <- panel_smooth( panel_clean, vars = "PZ", window = 3 )  # Smooth specific columns with decay weighting and a 5-year window panel_smooth_custom <- panel_smooth(   panel_clean,   vars    = c( "F9_01_REV_TOT_CY", "F9_01_EXP_TOT_CY", "F9_10_ASSET_TOT_EOY" ),   window  = 5,   weights = "decay" )  # Compute all fiscal health ratios on the cleaned, smoothed panel, # year by year so winsorization, z-scores, and percentiles are within-year panel_ratios <- compute_all_panel( panel_smooth_pz )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: following accounting ratios included package:

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Asset Revenue Ratio Definition: Total assets held per dollar annual revenue (asset intensity). Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: assets_rev = total_assets_eoy / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Savings Assets Ratio Definition: Cash savings share total assets; measures liquid composition asset base. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_assets = ( cash + savings ) / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Burn Rate Ratio Definition: End--year cash relative beginning--year cash. Values 1.0 mean cash drawn ; 1.0, accumulated. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_burn = cash_eoy / cash_boy

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Liquidity Ratio Definition: Measures organization’s ability cover current liabilities using cash savings. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_liq = ( cash + savings ) / ( accounts_payable + grants_payable )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Hand Definition: Absolute dollar amount liquid cash holdings (cash plus savings). Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_on_hand = cash + savings

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Current Ratio Definition: Measures short-term liquidity comparing current assets current liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: current = current_assets / current_liabilities  current_assets      = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable                       + inventories + prepaid_expenses current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Days Cash Investments Definition: Days operating coverage including investment assets net related debt. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: days_cash_inv = liquid_and_investment_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_and_investment_assets = unrestricted_net_assets + investments                                - ( land_buildings + mortgages_payable ) daily_expenses               = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Days Cash Hand Definition: Number days organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: days_cash_ops = liquid_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_assets  = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable daily_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Asset Ratio Definition: Proportion total assets financed liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: debt_assets = total_liabilities / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Equity Ratio Definition: Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_equity = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Net Assets Ratio Definition: Compares total liabilities total net assets (restricted unrestricted). See get_debt_equity_ratio() unrestricted-version. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: debt_netassets = total_liabilities / total_net_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Secured Debt Ratio Definition: Secured mortgages notes payable share total liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_secured = secured_mortgages_notes / total_liabilities

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Short Term Debt Ratio Definition: Share short-term liabilities relative total net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_shortterm = short_term_liabilities / net_assets  short_term_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Unsecured Debt Ratio Definition: Unsecured notes loans payable share total liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_unsecured = unsecured_notes_loans / total_liabilities

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Donation Grant Dependence Ratio Definition: Measures reliance contributions fundraising share total revenue. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: donations_rev = ( contributions + fundraising_revenue ) / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Earned Income Dependency Ratio Definition: Share total revenue earned program commercial income sources. Formula: Membership dues Part VIII line 1b excluded: already part total contributions (line 1h), get_donations_revenue_ratio() counts. Scope: 990 filers
code: earned_income = earned_revenue / total_revenue  earned_revenue = program_service_rev + royalties + other_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Equity Ratio Definition: Share total assets financed net assets (organizational equity). Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: equity = net_assets / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Administrative Overhead Ratio Definition: Share total expenses devoted management general administration. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_admin = mgmt_expenses / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Payments Affiliates Ratio Definition: Payments affiliates share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_affiliates = payments_to_affiliates / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Compensation Expense Ratio Definition: Total compensation employee-related expenses share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_compensation = ( officer_comp + disqualified_comp + other_salaries                           + pension_contributions + other_employee_benefits                           + payroll_taxes ) / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Fees Services Ratio Definition: Total fees paid outside professional services share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_feesforservice = ( mgmt_fees + legal_fees + accounting_fees + lobbying_fees                             + prof_fundraising_fees + investment_mgmt_fees                             + other_fees ) / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Grants--Others Expense Ratio Definition: Total grants paid domestic foreign entities share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_grants = ( us_org_grants + us_indiv_grants + foreign_grants )                   / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Member Benefits Expense Ratio Definition: Benefits paid members share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_membbenefits = member_benefits / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Fundraising Efficiency Ratio Definition: Cost raising one dollar contributions; lower values indicate efficient fundraising. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: fundr_eff = fundraising_expenses / total_contributions

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics

what: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: apply_transformations() central post-computation step called every get_*() ratio function. produces four versions ratio: raw (raw; unsuffixed metric column): unmodified computed ratio. winsorized (_w): outliers clipped bounds determined range argument winsorize proportion, via winsorize_x(). normalized (_z): distribution-appropriate transformation winsorized values, robustly standardized. transformation selected fitted via find_best_normalization() (stable interior non-NA, non-sentinel observations; "rank_normal" reference distribution also keeps winsorized tails), scored full vector via apply_normalization(). percentile (_p): integer percentile rank (1-100) based raw values, via dplyr::ntile().

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
code: apply_transformations(   x,   winsorize = 0.98,   offset = 0.001,   range = "np",   normalize_type = NULL )

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: x Numeric vector (computed ratio, transformation). winsorize Winsorization proportion 0 1 (default 0.98, clips 1st 99th percentiles "np" range). offset Sentinel offset applied fixed bounds (default 0.001). Observations clipped fixed bound stored just outside (lower bound minus offset, upper bound plus offset) remain identifiable _w column. range Character string describing theoretical range ratio. Controls lower upper winsorization bounds determined: "np" Negative positive (unbounded directions). Winsorizes symmetrically (1-winsorize)/2 1-(1-winsorize)/2 percentiles. Default behaviour. "zp" Zero positive. lower bound fixed -offset (flagging truncated--zero values) upper bound winsorize percentile full distribution. "zo" Zero one. bounds fixed (-offset 1+offset), flagging values outside [0, 1]. percentile-based clipping applied. "nz" Negative zero. upper bound fixed +offset lower bound 1-winsorize percentile. "lo;hi" Custom numeric range, e.g. "0;10". lower bound fixed lo - offset upper bound hi + offset. normalize_type Transformation type override passed find_best_normalization(). One NULL (auto-detect among "asinh", "logit", "rank_normal"), "asinh", "logit", "rank_normal", "hurdle" (never auto-selected). Default NULL.

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: named list elements raw, winsorized, z, pctile.

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: Winsorization Delegated entirely winsorize_x(), handles range codes, computes sentinel flags, returns winsorized vector alongside diagnostic metadata. Normalization (_z column) find_best_normalization() called first fit transformation parameters (type, scale constant, center, spread) stable interior winsorized distribution. apply_normalization() scores full original vector using fitted parameters. two-step design means fitted model can reused new data needed. Centering scaling use median/MAD, falling back mean/SD MAD zero. fewer three non-missing values model fitted z returned NA. Percentile rank (_p column) Integer percentile rank 1 100 based raw (pre-winsorized) values, computed dplyr::ntile().

what: Compute all fiscal health metrics year-by-year across a panel — compute_all_panel
title: Compute all fiscal health metrics year-by-year across a panel — compute_all_panel
text: panel-safe wrapper around compute_all() splits data year, computes every fiscal health metric independently within year's slice, stacks results. ensures winsorization bounds, normalization parameters, percentile ranks estimated cross-sectional distribution single year rather pooled multi-year distribution. year--year computation matters: compute_all() passes raw ratio vector apply_transformations(), fits winsorization bounds normalization model data receives. pooled panel distributions mixture N years, : ratio 95th percentile 2021 may rank 80th percentile pooled distribution 2022—2024 values higher. Winsorization clips pooled extremes, year-specific extremes. Z-scores centred scaled pooled moments. Splitting year computing avoids three problems: every _w, _z, _p column interpretable within-year percentile standardised value, exactly single-year call compute_all().

title: Current Ratio — get_current_ratio
text: current ratio widely used measure short-term liquidity commercial nonprofit finance. asks whether organization sufficient near-term assets meet near-term obligations without requiring asset sales, additional borrowing, emergency fundraising. nonprofits particularly important stress-test, grant revenue often arrives irregular cycles align payroll vendor payment schedules. Unlike quick ratio (get_quick_ratio()), current ratio includes prepaid expenses inventories, making somewhat generous (less conservative) measure liquidity. practice nonprofits, two ratios often move together since prepaid expenses rarely large share assets.

title: Current Ratio — get_current_ratio

title: Months of Liquid Unrestricted Net Assets (LUNA) — get_liquid_assets_months
text: Liquid unrestricted net assets (LUNA) measures many months operating expenses covered unrestricted net assets tied illiquid fixed property (net associated mortgage debt). refinement operating reserve ratio (get_operating_reserve_ratio()) precisely isolates liquid resources netting value fixed assets adding back portion financed mortgage debt (since debt reduces net equity encumbrance fixed asset).

title: Months of Liquid Unrestricted Net Assets (LUNA) — get_liquid_assets_months
text: (Unrestricted net assets - net fixed assets + mortgages payable) / (total expenses / 12). addition mortgage debt back numerator reflects logic organization sold building, receive net proceeds (market value minus mortgage balance) - mortgage liability already reduces unrestricted net assets. Adding back avoids double-counting encumbrance. formulation follows Zietlow et al. (2007) cited Calabrese (2013). differs get_operating_reserve_ratio() addition mortgages_payable numerator units: LUNA divides monthly expenses (months), operating reserve ratio divides annual expenses (multiple annual expenses).

text: Combined management fundraising expenses share total expenses. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded [0, 1]. Empirical range approximately [0.05, 0.50] operating nonprofits. title: Post-Depreciation Profitability Margin — get_profit_margin_postdepr
text: Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded 1.0; unbounded . typical range nonprofits approximately [-0.30, 0.30]. Extreme negative values may reflect major write-downs one-time capital expenses. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Healthy. -0.05 two consecutive years: Common vulnerability threshold. persistent gap post- pre-depreciation margins signals capital consumption requiring future capital expenditure. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: podpm = ( total_revenue - total_expenses ) / total_revenue

Default "np". Options: "np" (negative positive), "zp" (zero positive), "zo" (zero one), "nz" (negative zero), custom "lo;hi" pair (e.g. "0;10"). sanitize Logical (default TRUE). text: Net surplus deficit share total assets. Formula:   Definitional Range ROA unbounded directions. ratio zero means expenses exactly equalled revenues. Positive values indicate surplus years; negative values indicate deficit years. nonprofits, perpetual surpluses raise concerns mission prioritization perpetual deficits signal sustainability risk, meaningful range approximately [-0.20, 0.20] organizations years. Values can distorted small total asset bases (newly formed organizations) organizations whose assets consist almost entirely illiquid fixed property, making denominator poor proxy operational resource base. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even design. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Generally considered healthy – building modest reserves without appearing hoard resources. Sustained -0.05: Common threshold classifying organization risk (Greenlee & Trussel 2000, Keating et al. 2005). Asset structure matters: capital-intensive organizations mechanically produce low ROA even financially healthy. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Return on Assets — get_return_assets_ratio
text: Return assets (ROA) measures effectively organization uses entire asset base generate financial surplus. nonprofit context sometimes called return investment ratio, though "investment" means total asset base rather financial securities. positive ROA indicates organization ended year resources spent; negative ROA indicates deficit year. ROA useful longitudinal indicator - watching whether organization becoming less efficient generating surpluses per dollar assets time - cross-sectional comparisons within subsectors asset structures similar. frequently used dependent variable financial vulnerability models component composite fiscal health scores.

title: Return on Assets — get_return_assets_ratio
text: commercial accounting, ROA typically computed net income divided average total assets (mean beginning- end--year values), avoid distortion large mid-year asset changes. nonprofit literature generally uses end--year assets denominator (Greenlee & Trussel 2000, Keating et al. 2005) beginning--year balance sheet data reliably available 990 filings prior recent years, analytical focus stock resources time reporting rather flow average. numerator also differs commercial definition. Commercial ROA uses net income taxes. nonprofits, equivalent revenues less expenses (F9_01_EXP_REV_LESS_EXP_CY, Part line 19), IRS-reported summary figure change net assets adjustments. studies use Part XI reconciliation value instead, field 990-higher rates missing data. Part summary field available 990 990EZ forms used broader coverage.

title: Self Sufficiency Ratio — get_self_sufficiency_ratio
text: Measures whether program service revenue sufficient cover total expenses. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded zero; values 1.0 possible (indicate program revenue exceeds total expenses - surplus earned income alone). typical range nonprofits approximately [0, 1.5], values 1.0 since nonprofits depend contributed income. Benchmarks rules thumb SSR > 1.0: Fully self-sufficient program revenue; characteristic mature social enterprises fee-based service providers. SSR 0.50-1.0: Majority costs covered program revenue; moderate philanthropy dependence. SSR < 0.25: Heavily dependent contributed income; common advocacy organizations, arts nonprofits, grant-funded research entities. High SSR universally better – organizations serving low-income populations often require philanthropic subsidy design. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

Bounded negative infinity theory, practice empirical range nonprofits approximately [-0.30, 0.30] years. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal expected nonprofits operating close break-even. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Commonly considered healthy surplus range. -0.05 two consecutive years: Common vulnerability threshold (Greenlee & Trussel 2000). what: Normalize a numeric vector for multivariate analysis — normalize_x
title: Normalize a numeric vector for multivariate analysis — normalize_x
text: Convenience wrapper calls find_best_normalization() apply_normalization() single step. repeated application fitted model use functions directly. function winsorizes x according range winsorize, isolates stable interior (non-sentinel, non-NA values) fit transformation parameters, scores observations – including sentinels – using fitted parameters. prevents boundary pile-winsorization bounds distorting centering spread estimates ("rank_normal" reference distribution keeps winsorized tails; see ). Four transformation types supported: "asinh": inverse hyperbolic sine, scaled median absolute nonzero value stable interior. Defined zero, accommodates negatives, behaves like log tails. "logit": maps stable interior [0, 1] relative theoretical support, applies qlogis(). Suited variables bounded [0, 1] without heavy boundary mass. "rank_normal": rank-based inverse normal transform. Preserves ordering, distances. Robust irregular shapes mixed support. "hurdle": structural-zero mass receives 0; positive values transformed separately (rank logit) rescaled positive interval. vtype = NULL type auto-detected stable interior using heuristics based support range boundary mass ("hurdle" used requested explicitly). Scores stay bounded edges distribution preserve rank correlations raw data: "rank_normal" uses mid-ranks, pile-tied values (e.g. exact zeros, program-expense ratios exactly one) scored middle block, winsorized tails scored true quantile. "logit" clamps (1 - winsorize) / 2 quantiles strictly interior values, values 0 1 sent +/- log(2n). half transformed values tied, MAD zero robust standardization falls back mean/SD instead returning NA.
